Subject: Novaforge capacity probe - sustained & burst throughput for model inference

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking a look. Quick context: Novaforge is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for our customer-facing chat + embeddings pipelines. We have two model classes in the plan: a quantized 13B conversational model and a heavier 70B instruction model used for long-form summarization.

We attached a short sample_trace.json showing expected request mix over a 24h window (avg request size ~60 tokens generated, peaks with batch jobs producing ~8000 tokens across many requests). High-level asks:
- Can you give tokens/sec capacity estimates for each model on Redwood Dedicated (preferring A100/H100 options) at p95 < 300ms?
- What committed slab size would you recommend to meet a 2x peak headroom (we expect 3x ramp in 90 days)?
- Any immediate quick wins to reduce GPU footprint (quantization, caching, fallback models)?

Procurement wants a ballpark by EOD tomorrow so we can budget. Procurement timeline is ~30 days.

Thanks,
Ellen Park
Head of ML Ops, Novaforge

Subject: Re: Novaforge capacity probe - sustained & burst throughput for model inference

Ellen — thanks for the trace, this is a good amount to work with. Quick summary up-front, then the calc and recommendation below.

Summary (short):
- Sustained 24h baseline (~60 tok/req average): estimated aggregate ~9k tokens/sec.
- Peak burst windows observed: up to ~27k tokens/sec.
- With our recommended mix and runtime settings, to hit p95 < 300ms we recommend reserving a Dedicated pool equivalent to 32 A100-80GB GPUs (or 10 H100s) to cover steady + 2x headroom with burst lanes.

Key assumptions used in the calc:
- 13B quantized (q8/q4 variant) — measured on our runtime: ~420 tokens/sec per A100 GPU at 1k context, with batching and KV cache warm.
- 70B quantized (q4m) — ~85 tokens/sec per A100 GPU under the same SLO constraints.
- Average request token-gen: 60 tokens; arrival distribution from your trace.
- We budget a conservative batching window of 8–12ms for interactive traffic to keep p95 latency tight.

Detailed (estimates):
- Baseline tokens/sec: 9,000 tok/s (from sample_trace).
- If mix is 70% 13B / 30% 70B: equivalent GPU need (no headroom) =
  - 13B portion: 6,300 tok/s divided by 420 tok/s ≈ 15 GPUs
  - 70B portion: 2,700 tok/s divided by 85 tok/s ≈ 32 GPUs
  - blended baseline ≈ 47 GPUs
- To meet p95 < 300ms with headroom for spikes and model warmups we recommend: baseline reserve ≈ 32 A100s + burst pool that can add ~20 A100s (or equivalent H100s) quickly. That gives ~2x instantaneous headroom over baseline blended demand.

Operational notes and quick wins:
- KV/prefix caching is high impact for conversational flows with repeated system prompts — can cut 13B load by ~20% in steady-state.
- Offer fallback to a smaller 6–7B quantized variant for low-confidence generations (save ~2–3x GPU).
- If latency is the priority over throughput, moving latency-sensitive routes to H100s reduces GPU count by ~25% compared to A100 at cost premium.

Attachments: I dropped the numeric worksheet as novaforge_tps_calc.csv with per-model rows and slab math.

Next steps: happy to run a short internal sim with your trace and propose a 90/60/30-day commit phasing and a mutual action plan (MAP). If you want I can include a draft SLA and a DocuSign-ready MOP.

—Kimberly
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference

Adding operational details from the runtime perspective:

- Autoscale & burst behavior: Dedicated supports pre-warmed burst lanes — recommend configuring burst pool with a 60s warmup and 5–10s fast attach for small H100-backed instances. That lets you absorb short surges without moving the whole fleet.
- Batching policy: For the mixed workload we should set a small latency-first batch window (8ms) for chat routes and a larger throughput window (40–60ms) for long-form summarization jobs. This reduces token/sec demand during background jobs.
- Fallback routing: Configure policy to route requests to quantized fallback when queueing would push p95 above target. This keeps SLAs tight and preserves user experience.

Ops ask: if you can share which routes are latency-critical vs background, we’ll produce a split-slab recommendation (N live GPUs, M compute-only GPUs) and an ops runbook for cold-start/maintenance windows.

—Karthik
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
